info.title: OE Commerce Admin REST API
info.description:
Manage a single OE Commerce store's catalogue, orders, customers, and store configuration from
            your own back-office tooling. Building a customer-facing storefront instead? See
            [/docs/store](/docs/store).

            New here? [/guides/admin](/guides/admin) walks through getting a key and calling your first
            endpoint step by step - this page is the field-level reference to come back to afterward.

            ## Getting Started

            1. Click the **Authorize** button at the top of this page.
            2. Provide credentials - one of:
               - **Basic Authentication** - an Auth0 system-administrator's username/password.
               - **Bearer** - a JWT obtained via **Apps - Authentication**.
               - **API Key** via header `X-Commerce-Key` or `X-Storefront-Application-Key` - an Admin
                 Application Key in the form `sk_admin_{storeRef}_{secret}`. Admin keys are always secret
                 (server-to-server only) - there is no publishable admin key, and a request carrying a
                 browser `Origin` header is rejected outright regardless of any other credential supplied.
            3. For Basic/Bearer credentials (which carry no store reference of their own), also send
               `X-Store-Ref` with the store you're targeting.

            Once authorized, you can explore and test all available endpoints directly from this interface.

            ## Errors

            Failures use RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` field for
            programmatic handling, e.g. `admin_key_not_browser_safe`, `store_ref_invalid`, `unauthorized`.

            ## Rate Limits

            Requests are limited per Application Key (200/minute), falling back to per-IP if no key is
            present. A 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header.

featureKey is free text, not constrained to the FrontendFeature enum - the underlying store
already accepts custom keys beyond its 27 built-in features (matched at render time by theme
templates via a <feature name="..."> tag/attribute), so this same endpoint doubles as
"add/remove a custom feature grant"; there's no separate add-custom-feature action.

patch.summary: Update a frontend user role's settings
patch.description:
Only DisplayName, Description, SortOrder and IsActive are settable here - any field left out of
the request body keeps its current value. DefaultPriceListId has its own dedicated
PATCH .../default-price-list endpoint instead of being folded in here: it's nullable/clearable,
and on a partial-update body there's no way to tell "omitted" apart from "explicitly cleared" for
a field whose valid states already include null.

parameters.description: Unique row identifier of the frontend user role record

post.summary: Trigger a full Solr search reindex for the caller's own store
post.description:
Equivalent to Backoffice's Settings > Search Indexing > Index Products button -
    creates/verifies the store's Solr collection, then indexes its full product catalogue. This is
    a heavier, synchronous operation for a large catalogue; call it deliberately rather than on a
    tight polling loop.

200.description: HTTP status 200 if successfully processed, else returns HTTP status 400

post.summary: Bulk-import redirects for the caller's own store
post.description:
Accepts a JSON array of { OldUrl, NewUrl } items rather than Backoffice's raw CSV
    upload - a better fit for a programmatic caller. Rows that pass validation are always created
    even if other rows in the same payload fail; see the Errors property for a message per rejected
    line. Always resolves to the caller's own store - a global (null-StoreId) redirect is never
    created here.

requestBody.description: The redirects to import

200.description: HTTP status 200 with the created count and any per-line errors

post.summary: Create a redirect for the caller's own store
post.description:
An Admin API key is store-scoped, so this always creates a store-owned redirect - it

    subscription.

requestBody.description: JSON data model required to process request

201.description: HTTP status 201 if successfully processed, else returns HTTP status 400

IMPORTANT: DisplayOrder lives on the shared Extension row, not the per-store StoreExtension join
row (see Storefront.Common.Domain.Entities.Extensibility.Extension.DisplayOrder). The caller's
StoreId only scopes WHICH extensions are eligible for this reorder call (those enabled for the
caller's store) - it does NOT scope the mutation itself. Changing an extension's display order here
changes it for EVERY store on the subscription that has that extension enabled, not just the
caller's. This mirrors existing Backoffice behavior (ChangeDisplayOrderCommand) unchanged; it is not
a bug introduced by this endpoint and is not something this endpoint attempts to fix.

SuccessResponseModel.description:
Bare acknowledgement shape (`{ "success": true }`) returned by Store actions that don't have any other
data to report back - shared instead of each controller building its own anonymous object, so the OpenAPI
spec (and therefore generated SDKs) can document a real type instead of nothing.

enabled.description: Whether the role should have this feature.

priceListId.description:
Optional price list override for this specific feature, applied only when Enabled is true. Only
sets/replaces an override when supplied - omit or send null to leave any existing override as-is
(there's no way to explicitly clear an existing override back to null through this endpoint).

UpdateFrontendUserRoleRequest.description:
Partial-update request body for a frontend user role's settings. Any field left null keeps its
current value. To change the role's default price list (including clearing it), use the dedicated
